<Heading as={"h1"} className={"openapi__heading"}>
  {"Add time to internal clock"} <MarkerAddedInVersion version="8.11" />
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/clock/add"}
  context={"endpoint"}
></MethodEndpoint>

<MarkerStronglyConsistentExtension />

Moves the Zeebe engine's internal clock forward or backward by the given offset.
Unlike pinning, the clock keeps ticking in real time after the offset is added. If the
clock is pinned, it stays pinned and moves to the pinned time plus the offset.

Each request adds to the time of the clock, so adding `PT1H` twice moves the clock two
hours ahead. Use `POST /v2/clock/reset` to remove all added time and return the clock to
the system time.

The response contains the new time of the clock. The change reaches all partitions
shortly after it is accepted, so a request sent right after it may still use the previous
time.

<MarkerRequiredPermissions
  permissions={[{ resourceType: "SYSTEM", permissionType: "UPDATE" }]}
/>

<Heading id={"request"} as={"h2"} className={"openapi-tabs__heading"}>
  <Translate id="theme.openapi.request.title">Request</Translate>
</Heading>

<ParamsDetails parameters={undefined}></ParamsDetails>

<RequestSchema
  title={"Body"}
  body={{
    required: true,
    content: {
      "application/json": {
        schema: {
          type: "object",
          properties: {
            offset: {
              description:
                "The time to add to the clock, as an ISO 8601 duration in days, hours, minutes, and\nseconds (for example `PT1H` for one hour or `P1D` for one day). Use a negative\nduration such as `-PT1H` to move the clock backward. The request is rejected if the\nnew time would be before 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z.\n",
              type: "string",
              example: "PT1H",
            },
          },
          required: ["offset"],
          title: "ClockAddRequest",
        },
      },
    },
  }}
></RequestSchema>
